notes:
Checked on the fake backend only; no hardware was attached or run, and no human review or hardware test is claimed (reviewed_by is null). The upstream clone is Arduino C++ firmware plus a Python 2 VISA example; the driver neither installs nor imports it. The ScpiDriver opens a VISA resource (for the Arduino virtual serial port) or a TCP socket itself, so native names the card's ArduinoDAQ class for provenance only. The firmware has no readback command for the PWM outputs: voltage0 and voltage1 are the A0/A1 measurements of the same channels, matching the upstream write-then-read example (src/Examples/Meter/test.py:79-89); the fake models that loopback, but a bench must wire the outputs to the inputs for a write to appear in the state. The card's mock_strategy preferred a transcript; a strict replay cannot serve the varying gate and conformance sequences, so fake.py is a package lookup/stateful fake that answers only the commands registered in src/Examples/Meter/Meter.ino:33-43 and models the write effect, like the exemplar's fake. The fake's start values are placeholders; the identity reply is the firmware's own line (Meter.ino:78). No independent hardware e-stop is cited; at R1 (the cap.device.configure.v1 floor, above the card's R0 floor) the e-stop is a software binding that writes 0 V to both source channels. Not covered: the PWM output voltage cannot be read back independently of the A0/A1 inputs, and no instrument was used to confirm the wire syntax. Every Limit and Fact cites a line of the pinned clone; the gate reported no warnings.
